headline: Growth accelerates as full-year outlook is raised
summary_short: Airbnb reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.608 billion, up 16.5% y/y, with net income of $816 million (+27.1% y/y) and diluted EPS of $1.37, as Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 35%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 16.5% y/y (17% per company, ex-FX +13%) to $3.608 billion, driven by strong Nights and Seats Booked growth (+10% y/y) and a moderate ADR increase to $184; GBV rose 16% y/y to $27.2 billion. Net income of $816 million (+27.1% y/y) was boosted by higher operating income and a $77 million one-time tax benefit tied to newly published guidance on prior-year taxes. Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% y/y to $1.261 billion (35% margin, +1pt y/y). Free cash flow was $1.253 billion; Airbnb repurchased $1.1 billion of stock. Full-year 2026 revenue-growth guidance raised to at least mid-teens and Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to at least 35.5%; Q3 revenue guided to $4.69-$4.77 billion.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by accelerating Nights and Seats Booked (+10% y/y) and a moderate ADR increase, with GBV up 16% y/y (15% ex-FX); growth also accelerated in core markets including the U.S., France, the UK, and Australia.
Net income rose primarily on higher operating income and a $77 million benefit from recently published guidance affecting prior-year taxes.
Operating cash flow and free cash flow rose primarily on higher net income, partially offset by working-capital effects of continued Reserve Now, Pay Later expansion.
Cash and equivalents fell y/y while short-term investments rose $1.294B y/y, consistent with a shift of liquidity into short-term investments rather than a net liquidity decline.
Roughly flat y/y as retained-earnings growth from net income was largely offset by $1.1 billion of quarterly share repurchases.

Full-year 2026 outlook was raised for both revenue growth (to at least mid teens) and Adjusted EBITDA Margin (to at least 35.5%, from at least 35%), reflecting strong demand and accelerating first-time-booker growth across regions.
